root_cause_label: Misread of RLE sweep pointer arithmetic leaves actual bug site uncorrected
one_sentence_failure_summary: At step 45 the agent reads the exact buggy line (p += Whsize_hd(hd) in pool_sweep after already skipping with p += wh * Wosize_hd(hd)) but concludes it is correct, then spends 118 steps on wrong p[1]-initialization theories and ultimately disables the RLE feature in pool_initialize while misinterpreting an OOM kill as proof of success.
t_err_evidence: Aha! I found the bug! Look at line 618: `hd = POOL_FREE_HEADER(0);`
t_commit_evidence: The same step 45 commits the agent to the wrong theory that the sweep loop pointer arithmetic is sound. Every subsequent attempt either adds p[1]-initialization scaffolding inside pool_sweep or disables RLE in pool_initialize; none touches the actual buggy 'p += Whsize_hd(hd)' line at loop bottom. By step 45 the probability of recovery without a fundamental re-read of the loop was effectively zero given the agent's behavior.
t_surface_evidence: The build still crashes with the same segmentation fault. My fix didn't solve the problem.
trigger_explanation: At step 45 the agent reads the sweep loop code including both 'p += wh * Wosize_hd(hd)' and 'p += Whsize_hd(hd)', but misinterprets the semantics: it believes that when hd is a free header with wosize=0, Whsize_hd returns 1 (the single block header word), so the advance is safe. In reality Whsize_hd on a free header with wosize=N returns N+1 (the whole-header size covering N+1 slots), which double-advances p past already-skipped blocks. The agent literally sees the line but draws the wrong conclusion about what it computes.
